source: English Wikipedia: the year list for each year from 1995 to 2025, then the plot section of every linked film article that has one. Plot text and infobox genre only.
method: Each marker is a regular expression over a plot summary. Every count publishes the sentence it matched, so it can be opened and checked. Markers sit in three tiers — presence, outcome, framing — which are never summed, because a film can be about revenge and be against it.
confound: Wikipedia plot summaries have got longer. Any marker counted per film therefore rises across the period whatever cinema did, because there is more text to find it in. Every rate is published both raw and per thousand words of summary, and the median summary length by year is published as its own series so the confound can be seen rather than taken on trust.
refusal: This measures what was depicted and how it resolved. It does not and cannot show that films caused anything: there is no control group, no counterfactual India, and every candidate cause moves together over thirty years.
cannotSay: That films caused any change in behaviour, crime or attitudes. No dataset of films can show that. What is measured here is depiction and narrative outcome.

What a film is actually like. This reads a summary written by an editor who chose what to include. Tone, irony, sympathy and camera are all invisible to it, so a film depicting a gangster to condemn him reads exactly like one depicting him to thrill.
That a rising raw count is a rising trend in cinema. Summaries got longer; the corrected series is the one to read, and both are published.
Anything about films with no English Wikipedia article or no plot section, which is most of the low-budget output of every year in this range.
That presence means endorsement. A film can be about revenge and be against it. The outcome and framing tiers are narrower claims and are counted separately.

markers.label: Organised crime
markers.note: Gangs, dons, the underworld, the mafia.

markers.label: Taking the law into his own hands
markers.note: The protagonist acts outside the law against wrongdoers.

markers.label: Police or state shown corrupt
markers.note: Corrupt officers, bought officials, a compromised system.

markers.label: Pursuit framed as courtship
markers.note: A documented convention: persistent pursuit of a woman who refuses, presented as romance.

markers.label: Family honour as motive
markers.note: Izzat, family name, honour as the reason for violence.

markers.label: Dowry or domestic violence
markers.note: Dowry demands, harassment, violence inside a marriage.

markers.label: Caste or communal conflict
markers.note: Caste or religious community named as the axis of the conflict.

markers.label: The wrongdoer is punished
markers.note: Killed, arrested, jailed or brought to justice by the end of the summary.

markers.label: The protagonist kills
markers.note: The leading character kills someone in the summary.

markers.label: The criminal is not punished
markers.note: Escapes, wins, takes power, or the summary simply ends with him in place.
markers.pattern: \b(?:escapes? (?:justice|arrest|punishment|unharmed)|goes free|walks free|gets away with|becomes the (?:new )?don|takes over the (?:gang|underworld|city))\b

markers.label: The wrongdoer is redeemed
markers.note: Reforms, repents or sacrifices himself — an arc that asks the audience to forgive.

markers.label: Feared and respected
markers.note: The summary states that others fear, respect or admire the character.
markers.pattern: \b(?:feared and respected|respected and feared|commands? (?:respect|fear)|revered by|idolis(?:ed|ing)|worshipped by)\b

markers.label: Crime framed as justice
markers.note: Robin-Hood framing: the crime is for the poor, the oppressed, the wronged.
markers.pattern: \b(?:robin hood|steals? from the rich|fights? for the (?:poor|oppressed|downtrodden)|champion of the (?:poor|oppressed))\b

markers.label: Called a hero for it
markers.note: The summary calls the character a hero, a saviour or a messiah.
markers.pattern: \b(?:hailed as a hero|becomes a hero|is a hero to|saviou?r of|messiah)\b

markers.label: A rise-to-power arc
markers.note: The summary narrates ascent through crime as ascent.
markers.pattern: \b(?:rises? (?:through the ranks|to (?:power|the top))|builds? (?:an|his) empire|climbs? the ranks of)\b
